| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | *(see summary — defaults to publisher-level policy unless a journal-specific override was found)* |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | conditional |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 2 |
| **Summary** | Wiley/AJP-specific policy (per journal for-authors page): GenAI tools cannot be listed as authors and cannot be assigned responsibility for content. AI-generated images are not permitted on the cover or in articles. Tools used only for spelling/grammar/general editing are permitted if fully disclosed; authors remain fully responsible for all content including AI-assisted portions and must correctly reference supporting work. Final call on whether GenAI use is acceptable in a given manuscript rests with the editor. GenAI use in peer review itself is stated to be limited/restricted. This reads as journal-specific text consistent with Wiley's group-wide AI policy, not a generic publisher boilerplate link only — leniency rated 2/5 (permitted for light editing only, banned for content generation/authorship/images, editor has final discretion). |
| **Source URL** | https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/page/journal/10982345/homepage/forauthors.html |

**Current positioning (what the journal accepts now):** Broad-scope primatology journal; per its aims & scope it currently publishes across behavioral ecology, conservation biology, evolutionary biology, life history, demography, paleontology, physiology, endocrinology, genetics/molecular genetics, and psychobiology of nonhuman primates, plus a 'New Approaches' article type for emerging methods. A 2025/2026 special-issue call tied to the ASP 2026 conference symposium ('Looking at the Past, the Present and to the Future: What Is to Come for Primatology?') is soliciting submissions with a Jan 5 2026 deadline, explicitly inviting early-career primatologist contributions — signals current editorial appetite for retrospective/field-direction pieces alongside standard empirical work.

**Methods noted as welcome (qualitative — not a scored 0-5 table, see Methodological Preferences below):** behavioral ecology, conservation biology, evolutionary biology, life history/demography, paleontology, physiology/endocrinology, genetics/molecular genetics, psychobiology, review articles, commentaries, New Approaches (novel/methodological) papers, plenary addresses
